## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `94d09d50b58741e99575ea58c33c38c93e2bcbb0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: ui/packages/collaboration/src/index.ts, ui/packages/components/src/custom/index.ts + ui/packages/collaboration/src/useCollaborationTranslation.ts, ui/packages/collaboration/src/CommentThread.tsx, ui/packages/collaboration/src/PresenceAvatars.tsx, ui/packages/components/src/custom/mobile-dialog-content.tsx, ui/packages/components/src/index.ts, ui/packages/collaboration/package.json (exports map), ui/packages/components/package.json (exports map), ui/packages/components/vite.config.ts (dts emit), ui/packages/collaboration/README.md, ui/packages/components/README.md, ui/packages/i18n/src/useSafeTranslation.ts, ui/packages/plugin-form/src/ModalForm.tsx

Rendered 2026-11-08T05:37Z on PR #31387 (card #25921, batch 17: claim 6717134663, amendment 6717181444 at 2026-11-08T04:22Z). Net diff against `main` (merge base `8b904420`, the census base): 3 files, +26/−5; two code hunks each drop one `type` name from a named re-export list, the third file is the changeset. Every absence claim below was re-measured by this review on `origin/main` (`44a030bf`, fetched for this record) and on hotcrm `6961ab1`, by `git grep -w` over the whole tree; the PR body's account was not relied on. The twelve commits on `main` since the merge base touch neither package tree and add no changeset naming either operand.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set / public-surface change implied by the diff: exactly two type names leave two package entries, `CollaborationTranslate` from `@object-ui/collaboration` and `MobileDialogContentProps` from `@object-ui/components`, nothing else — right.** In `collaboration/src/index.ts` the re-export block from `./useCollaborationTranslation.js` keeps `useCollaborationTranslation` and `COLLAB_DEFAULT_TRANSLATIONS` and drops only the `type CollaborationTranslate` line; the module exports exactly those three names, so the other two stay whole. In `components/src/custom/index.ts` the list from `./mobile-dialog-content` becomes `export { MobileDialogContent }`; the module exports four names (`isInsidePopperLayer`, `usePopperAwareInteractOutside`, `MobileDialogContentProps`, `MobileDialogContent`), the first two already left the entry in the pending helpers batch, so the only new departure is `MobileDialogContentProps`. No value export moves; runtime emit is unchanged.
- **No second route to either name — right.** `collaboration/package.json` publishes one entry, `.`; `components/package.json` publishes `.` and `./style.css` only, so the per-file `dist/custom/mobile-dialog-content.d.ts` that vite-plugin-dts emits (`insertTypesEntry`, no type roll-up) is not reachable as a subpath. `components/src/index.ts` reaches the custom tree only through `export * from './custom'`; no other barrel or module re-exports either module (the whole-tree grep for `MobileDialogContentProps` hits only the sub-barrel and the declaring module). No published package star-exports either entry (zero hits for `export * from '@object-ui/collaboration'` or `'@object-ui/components'`).
- **Zero consumers through the barrel — right, re-measured.** `CollaborationTranslate` hits four files, all under `ui/packages/collaboration/src/`: the declaration, the entry, and `CommentThread.tsx` / `PresenceAvatars.tsx`, which import it from `./useCollaborationTranslation.js` by module path and use it only as the parameter type of the module-level helpers `formatTimestamp` and `statusLabel` — it appears in none of the exported interfaces `Comment`, `CommentThreadProps`, `PresenceAvatarsProps`. `MobileDialogContentProps` hits two files, the sub-barrel and the declaring module; `plugin-form/src/ModalForm.tsx`, the one outside reader of `MobileDialogContent`, never names the props type. hotcrm: 0 for both names, and hotcrm imports only `@object-ui/console`, `core`, `layout` and `react` — neither package at all. Positive controls on the same modules in objectstack: `useCollaborationTranslation` 18 files, `MobileDialogContent` 20 files. No pending `.changeset/*` names either operand; the two pending components changesets that mention `MobileDialogContent` name it as staying, and it stays.
- **Keep rule 3 (a kept export's signature reaches the name).** `CollaborationTranslate` is declared as the hook's return type indexed at `t`, so it is derived from `useCollaborationTranslation`, not the other way round; the hook's declared type (from `createSafeTranslation`, which returns `{ t, language }`) never names the alias — right, the rule does not hold it. `MobileDialogContentProps` is the explicit props type argument of the `React.forwardRef` call that declares `MobileDialogContent`, so in source the kept export is typed by the alias; this is the one point where the dev's measurement (the emitted declaration "spells its props out inline") could not be re-read here and is judged in ③.
- **Not taught — right.** The collaboration README teaches `useRealtimeSubscription`, `usePresence` with `PresenceUser`, `useConflictResolution`, `PresenceAvatars`, `CommentThread` with `Comment`; it names neither the translate type nor the hook. The components README teaches `initializeComponents`, `Button`/`Input`/`Card`, `usePageRegionPosture`, `resolveFieldReadFace` and the notification surfaces; no `MobileDialogContent*`. `content/docs/**`, `skills/**`, `docs/**`, `.claude/**`, `ui/skills/**` and every `CHANGELOG.md`: zero hits for both names. `Skills-docs: none` on the PR body is true of the tree.
- **In-package readers keep working — right.** Both declarations keep their module `export`; the two collaboration readers import by module path; the components tests touching the mobile dialog import `MobileDialogContent` only.
- **Check-runs on `94d09d50`, read at 2026-11-08T05:33Z: 52 runs — 17 success, 11 skipped, 24 in progress, 0 failure.** Success includes `Check Changeset` (which runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --self-test` and `--base MERGE_BASE`, `check-empty-changeset.mjs --base`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base`), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Build UI Deps`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, the three scoped lint lanes, `Type Check · source gates`, `Check PR Size`. Still in progress: `Test UI` (16 shards), `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`. The skipped runs are opt-in or push-only shapes. This record does not wait on the 24; their conclusions are the gate verdicts when they land.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/25921-collaboration-components-leftover-types.md`: `'@object-ui/collaboration': patch` and `'@object-ui/components': patch`, title `refactor(collaboration, components)!: …`, a **BREAKING** paragraph naming both names and the host they break, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, one `adr-0087: not-required (runtime-export-retired @object-ui/collaboration#CollaborationTranslate, @object-ui/components#MobileDialogContentProps) …` marker, and two `- FROM` lines — FROM spans 1:1 with the two package-qualified operands. Matches what the diff publishes: a non-protocol breaking narrowing of two published entries ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3; the same shape as the twenty-one pending `25921-*` changesets on `main`). Both packages sit at 18.3.0 in the one fixed group. One changeset for two packages is what amendment 6717181444 named; the gate reads package-qualified operands and `Check Changeset` is green on it. `Metadata-protocol: none` is true: no `packages/spec` schema, node type or stored shape names either operand.
- `Clause-②:` line: `no (narrowing)` at the start of a line on the PR body and in the changeset, read the same — the narrowing face, served here at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Correct: nothing in the diff is a published schema or a governed path (`record-recognisers --paths` on the file list decides no face by path and defers to this line).
- The changeset's "stays exported unchanged" sentence names `useCollaborationTranslation`, `COLLAB_DEFAULT_TRANSLATIONS`, `CommentThread`, `PresenceAvatars`, `MobileDialogContent` — all five remain in the two lists; true of the tree. Both TO expressions are total: the hook's return type indexed at `t` is exactly the alias's own definition, and `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef` applied to `typeof MobileDialogContent` yields the alias's members because the alias carries no `ref` key (it is built on `ComponentPropsWithoutRef` of the Radix content part).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 6717729234 (2026-11-08T05:27Z): `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`, `premise_still_valid: true`. Five process deviations (no assignees or labels on `pr_create`; shared checkout detached for the worktree; census control corrected to a grep-only control; branch not merged with `origin/main`) touch no file in the tree; the last is answered above — nothing on `main` since the base touches either package, and the queue rebuilds on `main`. Nothing to answer in the tree.
- PR-body flag "external npm hosts importing either type will fail to compile (未实测)": answered by the card's rules and the seat's amendment 6717181444; the changeset carries the BREAKING banner and a FROM/TO for each name, the card's accepted remedy. Not escalated.
- **Rule 3 for `MobileDialogContentProps` — answered, not escalated, with one caveat.** The dev's rule-3 reading rests on the claim that the emitted `MobileDialogContent` declaration spells its props out inline. This review is read-only and did not read the built `dist`; by the compiler's declaration-emit rule as this review reads it, an explicit alias type argument to `forwardRef` is printed by its alias name (the shadcn shape `ButtonProps & RefAttributes`), so the per-file `dist/custom/mobile-dialog-content.d.ts` most likely names `MobileDialogContentProps` — validly, since that module file keeps exporting the alias; only the entry stops re-exporting it. Judged on the rule's purpose rather than the unverified emit fact: a host holding the kept export loses no ability to name its props type, because the changeset's TO expression recovers it exactly, and `main` already carries the same move in the same package (`ResizableHandleProps` retired while `ResizableHandle` stays, TO `React.ComponentProps` of the component). The seat named this operand in the amendment with every claim rule standing. Should-fix, editorial, below the verdict line: see ④.
- `out_of_scope_findings`: `parseHHMM` (plugin-gantt `README.md` "Public exports" import list) and `Minimap` (plugin-designer `README.md` import line) are README-taught — verified on `main`; the amendment dropped both and the diff touches neither package. Nothing to file.
- Amendment fences hold: `components/src/ui/` is byte-identical (no path under it in the file list), no mobile fence, no pending `25921-*` changeset edited, no subpath entry, no `packages/**`. The newest `Claim:` on the card (6717134663) names `claude/project-thread-18lura`, the PR's head branch.

### ④ Design judgment

Read against the published spec on `main`: the two package READMEs, `content/docs`, `skills`, the entry comments in both barrels (the collaboration entry explains the i18n seam is exported "so a host can read the English defaults" and so later additions "translate through the same map"; the custom sub-barrel header says names left off a named list stay in their module for the package's own components), and the two cited modules in the live tree.

- **Does the narrowing take a declared capability away at the consumer?** No. The declared capability of the collaboration i18n seam is the hook and the English defaults map; both stay, and a host that wants to type the `t` it is handed writes the hook's return type indexed at `t`, which is the alias's own definition — or `SafeTranslate` from `@object-ui/i18n`, the translate shape that package does publish. `MobileDialogContentProps` is the props type of a component that stays exported in full; the props remain expressible as `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef` of the component, and no documented path (ModalForm's use, the README, the dialog docs) ever asked a host to name the alias.
- **Does it make the spec's own refusal real?** Neutral. Neither module refuses anything to a host; `CollaborationTranslate` exists, per its docblock, so in-package helpers "cannot drift" from the hook — an in-package alignment type, which the module keeps.
- **Implementation gap check (declared and not delivered, never narrowed at the consumer):** neither name is declared anywhere a consumer reads; both are delivered and unused. This is surface, not capability, so the rule has nothing to bite on.
- **Break attempts:** (a) a sibling package star-exporting either entry — none; (b) a subpath still carrying the names — both `exports` maps are closed (`.`, and `./style.css` for components); (c) a second route to the module — none in either root barrel or any sub-barrel; (d) an in-package reader importing through the barrel — none; (e) a public prop typed by the retired alias — none: `CommentThreadProps`, `PresenceAvatarsProps`, `Comment` and ModalForm never name it; (f) declaration emit after the retirement — the alias keeps its module-level `export`, so the emitted declaration of `MobileDialogContent` resolves whether it prints the alias by name or expands it; `Build UI Deps` is green on the head and `Type Check UI` / `Type Check · workspace` will say the rest; (g) a `main`-side drift since the census base — none in either package.
- **Should-fix (not blocking):** the changeset sentence "whose published declaration already spells the props out in full" asserts a fact about the built `.d.ts` that this review could not verify read-only and that the compiler's emit rule contradicts as read above. The sentence ships into `CHANGELOG.md`; it should say what is true either way — that the props stay recoverable as `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef` of `MobileDialogContent`, which the FROM/TO line already does. Prose only; the diff's accept-set and the remedy are right regardless.
- **Must-fix:** none.

The frontmatter (`patch` ×2), the title, the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` lines, the ADR-0087 marker with its two package-qualified operands, the BREAKING paragraph, the "stays exported unchanged" sentence and both `- FROM … TO …` lines are untouched; FROM spans stay 1:1 with the marker.
